subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should the public CLI/RPC/service `cron run` contract become uniformly non-consuming for one-shots and scheduler state, with scheduler-consuming behavior reserved to internal timer and gateway watcher paths?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes an existing public operator action rather than only repairing an internal implementation detail; source evidence supports the proposed safety model, but choosing the durable compatibility contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Treat all public `cron run` calls as verification runs that record an outcome without deleting one-shots or advancing scheduler-owned state, while retaining internal timer and watcher-terminal consumption.

options.title: Preserve consuming manual semantics
options.body: Keep the existing public force-run behavior and design a separate explicit safe-verification operation or opt-in preservation mode instead.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Treat all public `cron run` calls as verification runs that record an outcome without deleting one-shots or advancing scheduler-owned state, while retaining internal timer and watcher-terminal consumption.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged cron work owns adjacent next-run and maintenance invariants that determine the compatibility tradeoff.
